title: 1976-09-15_Dorothy_167.txt
concise_summary: In this entry PKD develops a theology of providential personhood: every individual chosen by God is not merely assigned a task but ontologically identical with it, as the Logos is identical with the Word made flesh. He argues that the bottom line of the entire Exegesis is not simply that God exists, but that God unfolds a vast, temporally extended plan through each individual's life -- a plan whose contours only become legible in retrospect. PKD then advances his central historical-eschatological claim: his novel Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said contains steganographic disclosure that our actual historical moment is A.D. 70 Rome, during the time of Acts of the Apostles, and that the 2-3-74 visions confirmed this truth rather than originating it. He concludes by reading his 27-year body of fiction as a dialectical arc resolved in Tears, and by positioning the present moment as the threshold of the Second Advent.
key_claims: The person chosen by God is not merely assigned a role but is ontologically the incarnation of that task: 'the person is the note + the role is the person,' analogous to the Logos being the Word come to life.
The ultimate revelation of the divine plan is self-referential: the psychopomp guiding the individual turns out to be the individual himself -- 'it is he who informs + guides himself.'

Reality is a tripartite amalgam of Ananke (chance), blind causal determinism, and sentient overrule (Nous), with the last having final authority and making 'corrections' that constitute evidence for the plan.

Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said contains hidden steganographic information disclosing that 1974 is actually A.D. 70 Rome -- the time of Paul and the Acts of the Apostles -- which PKD himself did not consciously know he had encoded.
The 2-74 / 3-74 visionary experiences and the publication of Tears are mutually confirming: each validates the other as testimony to the same underlying authentic reality.
PKD's 27-year sequence of novels constitutes a great dialectic whose question-and-answer structure is only resolved in Tears, making that novel's publication historically necessary.

autobiographical: PKD states that it was not until 1971 that he first sensed 'mysterious + supernatural entities, persons + powers at work protecting + guiding me.'

He describes hearing a cowboy tune as a child in 1933 that became a permanent memory, and then hearing it again decades later (he writes '1978' but likely means 1974 -- possibly a slip), understanding this recycling as part of a planned divine sequence.
He describes a dream in which a woman (apparently the singer associated with the cowboy tune) drives him in a vehicle and sings to him, alluding to 'another world.'

He recounts that the Xerox missive arrived in connection with the 2-74 / 3-74 experience and that someone (apparently hostile) had deciphered the theological material in Tears and sent it as a form of retaliation or 'backlash hit.'
He states that upon seeing the Golden Fish in 2-74 he 'remembered' precisely what the steganographic material in Tears states -- authenticating the vision by retroactive recognition.
He reflects that the entire 2-74 / 3-74 experience 'totally confirmed the truth of the revelation in Tears' and vice versa, describing them as 'of one piece.'

literary_self_ref: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said is read as steganographic disclosure: PKD 'showed, through Buckman, how the rigid iron framework of the world would have to be broken' -- a description that maps onto both the novel and reality.
PKD argues Tears depicts the 'true bedrock of reality' -- that we live in apostolic times, Rome A.D. 70 -- information he 'did not know that he had disclosed' until after publication.
He suggests Tears may blend the First and Second Advents: 'does Tears depict the First Advent? or does it not more accurately depict the second blended somehow with the first.'

He recommends reading 5-6 novels prior to Tears as a unit (including The Man in the High Castle, Eye in the Sky, Ubik, A Maze of Death, The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch) as a dialectical sequence whose question is resolved only in Tears.
A World of Talent is cited as a prior story where PKD 'touched on' the mystery of whether the veiled psychopomp figure is human, divine, or a mixture.
He asserts the publication of Tears was 'vital' because 'with it ended the entire 27 year sequence of questioning + answer' -- framing his whole career as a theological dialectic.
symbols_images: The vast tapestry (extended metaphor for the divine plan as an interwoven fabric across time, space, individuals, and nations)
The cowboy tune (a specific childhood memory from 1933, presented as a planted stimulus awaiting reactivation decades later)
The cave of quietness (the experience of understanding the plan is entering 'a huge cave of quietness' at the far end of which stands the blurred figure of the adviser)
The blurred / veiled figure (the psychopomp seen at the far end of the cave, eventually recognized as the individual's own mirror image)
The Golden Fish (the Ichthys symbol PKD saw during the 2-74 vision, triggering anamnesis of the Tears revelation)
The Xerox missive (an anonymous hostile document sent to PKD in early 1974, read as a 'backlash hit' by someone who deciphered Tears)
Rome as Platonic archetype (not a historical city but a recurring eternal form of tyranny against which authentic Christians are persecuted)
The razor's edge (the fine distinction between bait and opportunity -- they resemble each other as tests but are 'totally different in nature + purposes')
Robots acting on programmed instructions (PKD's self-description of humans as instruments of a higher plan, used without irony)
tensions: PKD writes '1978' when describing the year the cowboy tune would be heard again, but the surrounding context implies 1974; this may be a scribal error, a genuine future date PKD believed was still upcoming, or a deliberate distinction.

He asserts the plan cannot be fully comprehended ('there is no possibility of comprehending it') yet simultaneously claims to have discerned its contour through the 2-74 experience and Tears -- a tension between epistemic humility and revelatory confidence.

PKD raises the question of whether Tears depicts the First or Second Advent and cannot resolve it: 'does Tears depict the First Advent? or does it not more accurately depict the second blended somehow with the first' -- left open.
He acknowledges that whether 'everyone is utilized as parts of the plan I have no way to tell' -- universal versus particular election remains undecided.

The predestination problem is flagged but not resolved: the bait/opportunity schema implies predestination, which PKD notes parenthetically ('This would seem to make a case for predestination') but does not integrate into his broader theology of freedom and teaching.

The psychopomp revelation (the guide is the self) potentially collapses the distinction between human and divine, but PKD also lists Christ, Holy Spirit, and St. Sophia as separate mediating entities -- the two positions coexist without explicit reconciliation.
evidence_quotes: "The bottom line of all my exegesis is not just (sic) that there is a God, but that he has plans for us, which he unfolds through teaching + guidance as our lifetime progresses."
"The person is the note + the role is the person... the person is realing the animated embodiment of structure + purpose... like the Logos being the word come to life."
"The final mystery unfolds: it is he who informs + guides himself: he is himself his psychopomp, This is the last unveiling, the last secret."

"the true bedrock of reality beneath the spurious layers is that we live in apostolic times, specifically during the time of Paul + lure [Luke]... the actual time 70 AD the problem, Rome, + the solution, agape."

"we are living in 'Rome' (meant here as elong-term Platonic archetype) + the authentic Xtians have been persecuted + driven into hiding by the police establishment, but God is intervening now, + the old tyrannical system is to be thrown down this time."
uncertainty_flags: The year '1978' appears in the cowboy tune anecdote ('it knew then, in 1933 that the song would be heard again in 1978') but the 2-74 experience is the likely intended reference point; whether PKD means a future hearing still to come in 1978 or has made a slip for 1974 is unclear.
'Paul + lure' almost certainly means Paul and Luke (authors relevant to Acts), but the manuscript spelling is garbled; the identification of 'lure' as Luke is an inference.

The abbreviation 'Joint' in the reading-sequence list is ambiguous; it could refer to Dr. Bloodmoney (a 'joint' between two working-class communities) or another novel; the identification is not certain.

PKD refers to 'a world of talent' as a prior work where he touched on the psychopomp mystery; this appears to be the 1954 story 'A World of Talent' but could be a novel-length version or a different title misremembered.

The claim that 'someone evil' sent the Xerox missive after 'deciphering' Tears is presented as fact, but PKD himself acknowledges he does not know the sender's identity or true motivation; this conflates inference with knowledge.

PKD uses 'apostolic times' and 'A.D. 70' somewhat interchangeably, but A.D. 70 is the year of the destruction of Jerusalem, while the Acts period spans roughly A.D. 30-65; a scholar should note this historical conflation.
